questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Evaporation of a liquid can take place at temperatures below its boiling point.
2. Boiling is a surface phenomenon whereas evaporation is a bulk phenomenon.
3. Evaporation causes cooling.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Particles at the surface with enough energy escape at any temperature, taking heat with them, which is why wet clothes dry and sweat cools. Boiling is the bulk phenomenon and evaporation the surface one; the statement reverses them.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 1 Matter in Our Surroundings

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Acidic solutions have a pH greater than 7.
2. Pure water is neutral and has a pH of 7.
3. Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Acids give pH below 7 and bases above 7. Bacteria in the mouth make acids from sugar, and below pH 5.5 the enamel begins to corrode.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate.
2. Baking soda is sodium carbonate.
3. Gypsum is calcium sulphate hemihydrate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Plaster of Paris is CaSO4.1/2H2O, made by heating gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O, the dihydrate) at 373 K. Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO3), not sodium carbonate.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sodium and potassium are stored under kerosene oil.
2. Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.
3. Lead and mercury are good conductors of heat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Sodium and potassium react vigorously with air and water, so they are kept under kerosene. Lead and mercury are poor conductors of heat, unlike silver and copper.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Iron rusts even in dry air if oxygen is present, without any moisture.
2. Galvanisation is the coating of iron with a thin layer of zinc.
3. Brass is an alloy of copper and tin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rusting needs both oxygen and moisture. Zinc coating protects the iron even if scratched, as zinc is more reactive. Brass is copper plus zinc, while bronze is copper plus tin.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Diamond is a good conductor of electricity.
2. Graphite is the hardest known natural substance.
3. Buckminsterfullerene (C-60) is an allotrope of carbon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In diamond every carbon uses all four valence electrons in bonds, so there are no free electrons, and diamond is the hardest substance. Graphite is soft and conducting, and C-60 is a football-shaped allotrope.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Alkanes contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.
2. Ethene is an alkyne.
3. Ethyne has a triple bond between its two carbon atoms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Alkanes are saturated, alkenes have a double bond and alkynes a triple bond. Ethene (C2H4) is an alkene; ethyne (C2H2) is the alkyne.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is an exothermic process.
2. Photosynthesis is an exothermic reaction.
3. The reaction of quicklime with water is endothermic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Composting releases heat. Photosynthesis absorbs sunlight energy and is endothermic, while slaking of quicklime gives out so much heat that the beaker becomes hot.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 1 Chemical Reactions and Equations

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids.
2. Soaps clean by forming micelles that trap oily dirt at their centre.
3. Soaps form an insoluble scum with hard water.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. Hydrophobic tails of soap molecules enclose the grease in a micelle, while the calcium and magnesium salts of hard water react with soap to give scum, which is why detergents are used.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Robert Hooke first observed cells in a thin slice of cork.
2. The cell theory was proposed by Schleiden and Schwann.
3. The nucleus was discovered by Robert Hooke.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hooke saw the dead cell walls of cork in 1665. The nucleus was discovered by Robert Brown in 1831; Virchow later added that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 5 The Fundamental Unit of Life

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Prokaryotic cells lack a well-defined nucleus bounded by a nuclear membrane.
2. Prokaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles such as mitochondria.
3. Bacteria and blue-green algae are prokaryotes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Prokaryotes have a nucleoid and no membrane-bound organelles. Their lack of mitochondria and ER is the main contrast with eukaryotes.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 5 The Fundamental Unit of Life

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An animal cell swells when placed in a hypertonic solution.
2. A plant cell placed in a hypotonic solution takes up water and swells, but the cell wall prevents it from bursting.
3. Osmosis is the movement of water through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to lower.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: In a hypertonic medium water leaves the cell, so an animal cell shrinks. In a hypotonic medium water enters; the rigid cell wall of a plant cell resists bursting.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 5 The Fundamental Unit of Life

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Phloem transports food from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
2. Xylem is composed entirely of living cells.
3. Sclerenchyma cells are living and have thin cell walls.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Phloem carries food (translocation). Xylem is mostly dead cells, and sclerenchyma cells are dead with thick lignified walls, giving strength.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 6 Tissues

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Salivary amylase breaks down starch into sugar.
2. Pepsin digests proteins in the alkaline medium of the stomach.
3. Bile juice from the liver emulsifies fats in the small intestine.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Pepsin works in the acidic medium of the stomach, created by hydrochloric acid. Bile (made in the liver, stored in the gall bladder) breaks fat globules into small droplets and makes the medium alkaline.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.
2. In yeast, anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
3. Aerobic respiration releases less energy than anaerobic respiration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Glucose is first broken into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. Yeast then forms ethanol and CO2 without oxygen, whereas aerobic breakdown in mitochondria yields far more energy.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The human heart has four chambers.
2. The pulmonary vein carries deoxygenated blood.
3. The right atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The pulmonary vein carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium. The right side of the heart handles deoxygenated blood, so the right atrium receives blood from the body.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes
questions.h: Pulmonary is the odd one: artery carries bad blood, vein carries good blood.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Antibiotics are effective against viral infections.
2. Vaccines contain weakened or killed forms of the disease-causing microbe.
3. Penicillin was discovered by Louis Pasteur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Antibiotics act on bacterial processes, which viruses lack, so they do not work on viruses. Vaccines train the immune system without causing disease. Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 13 Why Do We Fall Ill

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mendel conducted his hybridisation experiments on fruit flies.
2. The sex of a human child is determined by the chromosome contributed by the father.
3. Human females have two X chromosomes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mendel worked on garden pea plants. The mother always gives an X, and the sex depends on whether the father's sperm carries X (girl) or Y (boy).
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 9 Heredity and Evolution
questions.h: Father decides: Y comes only from dad.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Auxin promotes cell elongation.
2. Abscisic acid promotes the growth of plants.
3. Cytokinins promote cell division.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor, which causes wilting and leaf fall. Auxin and gibberellins promote elongation, and cytokinins are concentrated in areas of rapid cell division.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 7 Control and Coordination

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Baking soda is used as an antacid.
2. Washing soda is used to remove permanent hardness of water.
3. Plaster of Paris is CaSO4.2H2O.
4. Bleaching powder is produced by passing hydrogen over dry slaked lime.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Plaster of Paris is CaSO4.1/2H2O, and bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Vinegar : Acetic acid
2. Curd : Lactic acid
3. Tomato : Oxalic acid
4. Tamarind : Citric acid
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Pairs 1 to 3 are correct. Tamarind contains tartaric acid; citric acid is found in citrus fruits such as lemon and orange.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Graphite is used as a lubricant.
2. Ethene is a saturated hydrocarbon.
3. Diamond is a good conductor of electricity.
4. Ethanol is a hydrocarbon.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only 1 is correct. Graphite layers slide over one another. Ethene has a double bond (unsaturated), diamond has no free electrons, and ethanol contains oxygen, so it is not a hydrocarbon.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Mitochondria are the sites of release of energy in the form of ATP.
2. The rough endoplasmic reticulum has ribosomes attached to its surface.
3. Lysosomes digest worn-out cell organelles and foreign material.
4. The Golgi apparatus is involved in packaging and dispatch of materials.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. These are the textbook functions of the four organelles.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 5 The Fundamental Unit of Life
questions.h: Mitochondria = power; Lysosome = suicide bag/waste disposal; Golgi = post office.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Insulin : Pancreas
2. Thyroxine : Thyroid
3. Adrenaline : Pituitary
4. Growth hormone : Adrenal
How many of the above pairs are correct?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. Adrenaline comes from the adrenal glands and growth hormone from the pituitary; the two are swapped in the pairs.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 7 Control and Coordination

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stomata are present only on the lower surface of every leaf.
2. Xylem transports food prepared in the leaves.
3. Chlorophyll absorbs mainly green light.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None is correct. Stomata occur on both surfaces in many leaves; xylem carries water and minerals while phloem carries food; chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light and reflects green.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Aluminium objects resist corrosion in air even though aluminium is a reactive metal.
Statement-II: Aluminium forms a thin, protective layer of its oxide on the surface.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The aluminium oxide film is tough and non-porous, so it seals the metal beneath from further reaction with air.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Ionic compounds have high melting and boiling points.
Statement-II: Ionic compounds conduct electricity in the molten state.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: High melting points come from the strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions. Conduction in the molten state is a separate property which arises because the ions become free to move.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Vaccination protects a person against a particular disease.
Statement-II: Vaccines contain active and fully virulent forms of the disease-causing microbe.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Vaccines contain weakened or killed microbes, or parts of them, which trigger an immune response without causing the disease.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 13 Why Do We Fall Ill

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Diamond is a good conductor of electricity.
Statement-II: In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three others, leaving one free electron per atom.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Diamond has no free electrons, as all four valence electrons form bonds, so it is an insulator. In graphite the fourth electron is free, which gives conductivity.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The sex of a human child is determined by the father.
Statement-II: The father produces two types of gametes, carrying X or Y chromosome, while the mother produces only X-bearing eggs.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A sperm with X gives a girl and one with Y gives a boy, while every egg carries X. The father's gamete type decides the sex.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 9 Heredity and Evolution

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Common name)
A. Baking soda
B. Washing soda
C. Bleaching powder
D. Plaster of Paris
List-II (Formula)
1. CaOCl2
2. NaHCO3
3. CaSO4.1/2H2O
4. Na2CO3.10H2O
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, washing soda is hydrated sodium carbonate, bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, and Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Metal)
A. Aluminium
B. Mercury
C. Iron
D. Zinc
List-II (Ore)
1. Cinnabar
2. Bauxite
3. Zinc blende
4. Haematite
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Bauxite gives aluminium, cinnabar (HgS) gives mercury, haematite (Fe2O3) gives iron, and zinc blende (ZnS) gives zinc.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Vitamin)
A. Vitamin A
B. Vitamin C
C. Vitamin D
D. Vitamin B1
List-II (Deficiency disease)
1. Scurvy
2. Rickets
3. Night blindness
4. Beriberi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Vitamin A is needed for vision in dim light, vitamin C for connective tissue, vitamin D for calcium absorption in bones, and thiamine (B1) for nerve and muscle function.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 13 Why Do We Fall Ill / Ch 15 Improvement in Food Resources; NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6
questions.h: A for eyes at night; C for scurvy (sailors' limes).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Disease)
A. Malaria
B. Tuberculosis
C. Dengue
D. Ringworm
List-II (Type of causative organism)
1. Bacterium
2. Virus
3. Protozoan
4. Fungus
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium (protozoan), tuberculosis by a bacterium, dengue by a virus, and ringworm by a fungus.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 13 Why Do We Fall Ill

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Cell organelle)
A. Mitochondria
B. Lysosome
C. Ribosome
D. Golgi apparatus
List-II (Function)
1. Protein synthesis
2. Release of energy
3. Digestion and waste disposal
4. Packaging and dispatch of materials
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Mitochondria release energy as ATP, lysosomes digest waste, ribosomes make proteins, and the Golgi apparatus modifies, packages and dispatches products.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 5 The Fundamental Unit of Life

questions.q:
Arrange in decreasing order of chemical reactivity:
1. Copper
2. Zinc
3. Magnesium
4. Iron
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: The reactivity series runs K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au. A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one from its salt, which is how the order is established.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals
questions.h: K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb H Cu Hg Ag Au

questions.q:
Arrange in the correct order the path of deoxygenated blood returning from the body to the lungs:
1. Right ventricle
2. Right atrium
3. Pulmonary artery
4. Lungs
Select the correct answer:
questions.e: The vena cava empties into the right atrium, which fills the right ventricle. The ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs, where it picks up oxygen.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes

questions.q: When carbon dioxide gas is passed through lime water, the lime water turns milky because
o: carbonic acid is formed in large quantity
questions.e: Ca(OH)2 + CO2 gives CaCO3, which is insoluble in water and appears as a milky suspension. On passing excess CO2 the milkiness disappears due to formation of soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q: Which one of the following solutions has the highest pH?
questions.e: Baking soda solution is mildly basic (pH around 8), pure water is neutral, milk is very slightly acidic, and lemon juice is clearly acidic.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 2 Acids, Bases and Salts

questions.q: An element has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. The number of neutrons in its nucleus is
questions.e: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 23 - 11 = 12.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 4 Structure of the Atom

questions.q: An element X has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 2. It is most likely to be
o: a divalent non-metal that gains two electrons
a divalent metal that loses two electrons
questions.e: With two electrons in the outermost shell, the atom is magnesium and loses them to attain the stable octet of the next inner shell. It therefore forms X2+ ions.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 4 Structure of the Atom; NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 5

questions.q: When ethanol is warmed with ethanoic acid in the presence of a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid, the product is
questions.e: This esterification forms ethyl ethanoate and water, with the sulphuric acid acting as a dehydrating agent and catalyst. Esters are responsible for fruity smells and are used in perfumes.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q: In a homologous series of carbon compounds, successive members differ in molecular mass by
questions.e: Each member differs from the next by a CH2 unit, whose mass is 12 + 2 = 14 u.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 4 Carbon and its Compounds

questions.q: Which one of the following metals can be cut with a knife?
questions.e: Alkali metals such as sodium, lithium and potassium are soft because of weak metallic bonding. Most other metals, including iron and copper, are hard.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 3 Metals and Non-metals

questions.q: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from
questions.e: Light energy splits water molecules into hydrogen and oxygen. The hydrogen reduces carbon dioxide to carbohydrate, and oxygen escapes through stomata.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes
questions.h: O2 comes from H2O, not CO2.

questions.q: The opening and closing of the stomatal pore is controlled by
o: epidermal cells, which release carbon dioxide
guard cells, which swell or shrink as they take up or lose water
questions.e: When water flows into the guard cells they swell and the pore opens; when they lose water they become flaccid and the pore closes. This regulates both gas exchange and transpiration.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes

questions.q: Reflex actions, such as withdrawing the hand on touching a hot object, are mainly controlled by the
questions.e: The reflex arc runs from receptor to sensory neuron to the spinal cord and then to a motor neuron and effector, without waiting for the brain. This saves crucial time.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 7 Control and Coordination

questions.q: The basic filtering unit of the human kidney is the
questions.e: Each kidney has about a million nephrons, in which the glomerulus filters blood and the tubule reabsorbs useful substances like glucose and water, leaving urine.
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 6 Life Processes

questions.q: In Mendel's cross between pure tall and pure short pea plants, the F2 generation shows tall and short plants in the ratio
questions.e: All F1 plants are tall because tallness is dominant. When F1 plants self-fertilise, the recessive short trait reappears in one quarter of F2. 1:2:1 is the genotypic ratio, and 9:3:3:1 is for two traits (dihybrid cross).
questions.s: NCERT Class 10 Science, Ch 9 Heredity and Evolution

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have
o: the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
the same mass number but different atomic numbers
different numbers of electrons but the same number of protons
questions.e: Isotopes share atomic number but differ in mass number because of different neutron counts (for example, protium, deuterium and tritium). Atoms with the same mass number and different atomic numbers are isobars.
questions.s: NCERT Class 9 Science, Ch 4 Structure of the Atom
